tasks.short: Design and validate clinical databases and logic checks.

steps.what: Design clinical databases.
Design logic checks for the databases.
Testing logic checks on known cases.
Review testing failures of the checks.
Accept the validated clinical databases.
File the accepted clinical databases.

tasks.design: The data manager designs the clinical databases and the logic checks. The {DATA_PLATFORM} runs known cases they already wrote, if its own check runner can do that. They review every failure and accept the databases. The file stores that version. Nothing designs a check and nothing changes site data.
tasks.previous_blocker: Designing a check is a judgement about the protocol. The same check is then clicked through by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: The clinical system's own check runner can execute cases the data manager has already written.
tasks.still_hard: A check that does not match the protocol still has to be judged by the data manager.
tasks.human_edge: The data manager designs the databases and the checks, and accepts them after the test failures are reviewed.

ambition.what: Retest the logic checks on the day a check changes, rather than only before a lock.

tasks.altitude: Designing the databases and the checks stays with the data manager. The file holds them only after they accept the tested version.

reach.task: Build on a database the data manager validated
reach.learn: The checks were designed by the data manager

evidence.claim: Designing a logic check is a judgement about the protocol. A test run can execute cases the person already wrote. It does not design the check.

Castor flags discrepancies at entry, extracts source data with confidence scores, and a person signs off. It also manages queries. That is the runtime of a check a person already designed, not the design of the database.

A medicines-agency guideline expects validated edit checks, forbids a sponsor from changing investigator data without authority, expects a secure audit trail, and says a model may raise a query but must not correct the record. Rules specific to AI are deferred.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the protocol fields are known and ends when the accepted databases are on the file. Designing the checks stays with the data manager. A model does not change investigator data.

The fields are the check name, the case the data manager wrote, the pass or fail, and their acceptance. They produce the check. If the system's runner cannot execute a case, they test it. Nothing invents a check.
The prior treats the task as amplify. The steps agree on the design. They disagree only about running cases the data manager has already written, and about filing the version they accept.
Upkeep is keeping the known cases aligned with the checks.
unknowns: Whether the clinical system can already run a scripted case.
Which protocol sections the checks must cover.
research_questions: Can the clinical system already run a scripted case?
Which protocol sections must the checks cover?

already_counted.description: Designing logic checks for the databases stays in full inside that step

incremental.description: Keep the known cases aligned with the checks

approvals.approved_version: clinical databases the data manager accepted after designing the checks and reviewing the test failures

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the clinical system cannot run the known cases, that testing stays, and the low end is the design of the databases and the checks, which stay either way. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Process clinical receipt, entry, verification, and filing.

steps.what: Process the clinical receipt of structured files.
Process clinical entry of narrative information.
Run verification on the clinical information.
Review verification exceptions before filing.
Accept the clinical information for filing.
File the accepted clinical information.

tasks.design: A structured file is received by the {DATA_PLATFORM} import the data manager has already configured. They still enter narrative information, because a model must not write site data. Native edit checks verify the fields. They review exceptions, accept the information, and only then is it filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Receipt, entry, and filing are often retyped between a file, a screen, and a tracker.
tasks.enabler_now: The clinical system can import a structured file and run edit checks it already has.
tasks.still_hard: Narrative source text still has to be entered and read by a person. A wrong import must not overwrite investigator data.
tasks.human_edge: The data manager enters narrative information and accepts the file. Structured receipt and field verification do not.

ambition.what: File a verified structured receipt on the day it arrives, rather than in a weekly batch.

tasks.altitude: Narrative entry and the acceptance stay with the data manager. Structured receipt is an import. The file holds only the version they accept.

reach.task: Use a receipt the data manager has filed
reach.learn: The narrative was entered by the data manager

evidence.claim: Castor flags discrepancies at entry, extracts source data with confidence scores, and a person signs off. It also manages queries. That is the runtime of a check a person already designed, not the design of the database.

A medicines-agency guideline expects validated edit checks, forbids a sponsor from changing investigator data without authority, expects a secure audit trail, and says a model may raise a query but must not correct the record. Rules specific to AI are deferred.
Trial health data is special-category data. Research processing needs the research condition and the accompanying safeguards.
Structured receipt can be an import. Narrative entry stays with a person because the record must not be rewritten by a model.

assumptions: The workflow starts when a file or a narrative source arrives and ends when the accepted information is filed. The data manager enters narrative text. Nothing writes site data.

The fields are the file name, the visit, the field value, the check result, and their acceptance. The site or the lab produces the source. If the import fails, they enter the structured fields. A missing narrative is typed by them.
The prior treats the task as automate. The steps agree on structured receipt and on field verification. They disagree by keeping narrative entry and the acceptance.
Upkeep is keeping the import map aligned with the file layout.
unknowns: Whether sites still send paper or a structured feed.
Whether the clinical system already has an import for that feed.
research_questions: Do sites still send paper, or a structured feed?
Does the clinical system already import that feed?

already_counted.description: Narrative entry of clinical information stays in full inside that step

incremental.description: Keep the import map aligned with the file layout

approvals.approved_version: clinical information the data manager accepted after narrative entry and the verification review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If sites still send narrative on paper, that entry stays, and the low end is the narrative entry and the exception review, which stay either way. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Generate data queries from checks and omissions.

steps.what: Generate queries from validation checks.
Read omissions identified during entry.
Draft queries that resolve the identified problems.

loop.purpose: Draft a query from a free-text omission.
loop.input: The omission text and the validation check that fired.
loop.output: A proposed query the data manager has not sent.
loop.check: The data manager accepts or rewrites the query. It must not change site data.
loop.stop: Stop when they accept or reject. The draft never sends itself and never writes the clinical record.
loop.why_not_simpler: The omission is prose. A field fill cannot phrase the question to the site.

steps.what: Accept the queries that resolve the problems.
Send the accepted queries.

tasks.design: Native validation checks on the {DATA_PLATFORM} open a query for a structured failure. The data manager still reads a free-text omission. A draft query is proposed from that text and they rewrite it. The {EMAIL} sends only the wording they accepted. The draft never writes the clinical record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Query text is copied out of a check listing into a mailbox, and the same omission is re-read later.
tasks.enabler_now: The clinical system can open a query from a validation check it already runs, and a bounded draft can phrase a question from omission text.
tasks.still_hard: The data manager still has to judge whether the question is fair to the site. A wrong query must not change the record.
tasks.human_edge: The data manager reads the omission and accepts the query. The send is that accepted wording and nothing else.

ambition.what: Send a query the day the omission is confirmed, rather than in a weekly batch.

tasks.altitude: Reading the omission and accepting the query stay with the data manager. A structured check can open its own query. The message is only the version they accepted.

reach.task: Answer a query the data manager accepted
reach.learn: The wording was accepted by the data manager

evidence.claim: Castor flags discrepancies at entry, extracts source data with confidence scores, and a person signs off. It also manages queries. That is the runtime of a check a person already designed, not the design of the database.
Clinical Data Studio does automated listings review, query management, reconciliation, and audit-trail review.

A medicines-agency guideline expects validated edit checks, forbids a sponsor from changing investigator data without authority, expects a secure audit trail, and says a model may raise a query but must not correct the record. Rules specific to AI are deferred.
EU rules have required AI literacy since February 2025 for people who use a system that drafts text. The person must be able to accept or reject the draft.

assumptions: The workflow starts when a check fires or an omission is seen, and ends when the accepted query is sent. The data manager accepts the wording. Nothing writes site data.

The fields are the check id, the field, the omission text, the query text, and their acceptance. The entry step produces the omission. If the text is too thin, they write the query. The draft never sends itself.
The prior treats the task as automate. The steps agree on opening a query from a structured check. They disagree by keeping the reading, the rewrite, and the acceptance.
Upkeep is keeping the query phrases aligned with the checks, and reviewing drafts that the person rejects.
unknowns: Whether the site expects the query by mail or in the clinical system.
Which omission fields are free text.
research_questions: Does the site expect the query by mail or in the clinical system?
Which omission fields are free text?

already_counted.description: Reading omissions identified during entry stays in full inside that step

incremental.description: Review drafts the data manager rejects, and keep query phrases aligned with the checks

approvals.approved_version: queries the data manager accepted after reading the omission

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the omission text is too thin to draft from, the person writes the query, and the low end is reading the omission and accepting the wording, which stay either way. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.short: Develop data management plans and database locks.

steps.what: Develop management plans for coding.
Address reporting and transfer in the plans.
State database locks in the plans.
Check lock criteria against the plans.
Accept the management plans and the locks.
Apply the accepted database locks.

tasks.design: The data manager writes the management plan: coding, reporting, transfer, and the database-lock rules. The {DATA_PLATFORM} counts the criteria they named, such as open queries and a matching record count, if those are already fields. They accept the plan and the lock. Only that accepted lock is applied. Nothing decides that the database may lock.
tasks.previous_blocker: The plan is rewritten for each project, and the lock is clicked after a manual count of open queries.
tasks.enabler_now: Open queries and record counts are fields the clinical system can already count.
tasks.still_hard: The lock rules are a judgement. A count does not decide that the database may lock.
tasks.human_edge: The data manager writes the plan, sets the lock rules, and accepts the lock after seeing the criteria.

ambition.what: Apply a database lock on the day the criteria they set are met.

tasks.altitude: Writing the plan and the lock rules stays with the data manager. The lock is applied only after they accept the criteria result.

reach.task: Keep a database the data manager has locked
reach.learn: The lock rules were set by the data manager

evidence.claim: EU clinical-trial rules require verifiable records, and the master file is kept for 25 years.

A medicines-agency guideline expects validated edit checks, forbids a sponsor from changing investigator data without authority, expects a secure audit trail, and says a model may raise a query but must not correct the record. Rules specific to AI are deferred.
The data manager sets the lock rules. A count of open queries is a field check. It does not decide the lock.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the protocol is known and ends when the accepted lock is applied. The data manager writes the plan and accepts the lock. The criteria count uses fields the system already stores.

The fields are the plan section, the lock rule, the open-query count, the record count, and their acceptance. They write the rule. If a criterion is not a field, they count it. Nothing locks the database on its own.
The prior treats the task as automate. The steps agree that a criteria count can be a field check. They disagree by keeping the plan, the lock rules, and the acceptance.
Upkeep is keeping the lock criteria aligned with the plan.
unknowns: Which criteria the sponsor requires before a lock.
Whether those criteria are already fields in the clinical system.
research_questions: Which criteria does the sponsor require before a lock?
Are those criteria already fields in the clinical system?

already_counted.description: Developing the management plans for coding stays with the data manager

incremental.description: Keep the lock criteria aligned with the plan

approvals.approved_version: database locks the data manager accepted after the criteria check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the lock criteria are not fields in the system, the count stays manual, and the low end is writing the plan and the lock rules, which stay either way. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The data manager still designs the databases and the logic checks, still enters narrative information, still accepts every query before it is sent, and still writes the management plan and the lock rules. A test run, a structured import, a field check, and a lock-criteria count are the machine parts. A query is sent only after they accept that wording. A lock is applied only after they accept the criteria.
reach: A health informatics specialist builds on a database the data manager validated
A clinical monitor answers a query the data manager accepted
skills_to_grow: Designing the logic checks rather than having them proposed
Entering narrative information rather than letting a model write it
Accepting a query before it is sent
role.ambitious_version: Every filed database is one the data manager designed, and every query that leaves is one they accepted.
